verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack five Hemorrhage bleeds and press R; you win by chain-CCing him with Q into W before he gets there.

brief.thesis: Darius wins by wrapping E (Apprehend) onto you or stacking five Hemorrhage bleeds for an enraged, lethal Q/R combo. Volibear wins the same trade pattern by landing Q (Thundering Smash) to stun him on engage, then double-tapping W (Frenzied Maul) for the bonus damage and heal before he can stack bleeds back. This is reflected in the numbers: 52.3% Volibear win rate over 2,752 games, ahead of his 48.9% baseline, with both lane kills and solo-kill edge favoring Volibear.

theirWindow.what: He is close to enrage threshold and his Q (Decimate) heal off you gets stronger — back off and let stacks fall off rather than extending the trade.

yourWindow.what: Apprehend cooldown is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s versus your Q at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s — walk up and force a stun-lock trade with Q into W while he has no pull to punish your approach.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: Taken in 70.1% of games at 52% win rate — the extra sustain outlasts his Q wind-up pokes and bleed ticks through the early trades.

boots.why: 56% pick rate at 51.2% win rate — the flat damage reduction blunts his auto-attack resets and Hemorrhage stacking.

core.why: First item in the highest-winrate path (57.1% over 312 games) — gives the attack speed to stack your own passive before he can enrage.
Reduces your Q/W cooldowns further, letting you stun-and-heal loop faster than his Apprehend resets.

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken in the top rune page (33.5% pick, 52.1% win rate) — ramping attack speed lets your passive proc faster in extended trades, which matters since Darius wants short, decisive bleed stacks and you want long ones.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 79.9% of games at 52.8% win rate — OP.GG's own read confirms Ignite lets you cap his healing from Q (Decimate) during all-ins and close out kills he'd otherwise survive on low HP.

playing.title: Open with Q, not W
playing.detail: Thundering Smash's stun on his first engage locks him out of his own Q wind-up — land this before he can swing his axe.

playing.title: Double-tap W for the heal
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul's second cast on a marked target heals you — chain it immediately after your Q stun to win the sustain race against his bleed.

playing.title: Track his E range at 535
playing.detail: Apprehend pulls from 535 range on a 26-16s cooldown depending on rank — don't stand at that distance when it's up, or he resets neutral trades into forced ones.

playing.title: Poke with E between fights
playing.detail: Sky Splitter's 1200 range slow lets you chip him down safely; this is the exact poke OP.GG's own notes call out for gaining lane control.

playing.title: Reset bleed stacks by disengaging
playing.detail: Hemorrhage stacks decay over 5 seconds — if you're above 3 stacks, walk out of range rather than trading through to his enrage threshold.

playing.title: Save R for a committed all-in
playing.detail: Stormbringer's long cooldown (160s at rank 1, down to 110s) means you only get one swing per fight window — use it to close distance when his E is down, not to start poke.

playing.title: Punish his cooldowns, not his HP bar
playing.detail: His kit resets off kills and stacks, not just damage — all-in when his Apprehend and Q are both on cooldown rather than waiting for a specific health threshold.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own tactical read, not sourced from the data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not get pulled by Darius’s (E). Bring Ignite to lane aggressively or use a couple of [E] pokes to gain lane control.
